subject: Service interruption in US/EU/APAC regions — traffic shift checklist & SLA bridge
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Jesse Park <jesse@heliobank.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Dec 2029 08:12:00 +0000
Subject: Service interruption in US/EU/APAC regions — immediate guidance

Hi Jesse,

TL;DR: We're seeing a regional network disruption at our cloud provider affecting parts of US, EU and APAC that is increasing latency and causing intermittent request failures for some customers. Our on-call has applied automated fallbacks; below are short, actionable steps your SREs can apply in the next 10–30 minutes to reduce impact.

Immediate customer actions (priority order):
- Switch API traffic to a single healthy region: console link below (set region preference to us-west or us-central).
- Reduce max_tokens and target a smaller model variant (e.g., redwood-medium) to reduce per-request compute and latency spikes.
- Increase client-side retry backoff to 800ms exponential, limit retries to 2 to avoid higher tail load.
- If you use a weighted routing policy, push 100% to the fallback region for now and lower concurrency (keep batch_size <= 4).

Helpful console link: https://app.redwood.ai/console/projects/heliobank/routing
Incident status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2029-12-21-3

We've attached a one-page traffic-shift snippet you can paste into your infra as well (traffic-shift-snippet.txt). I'm copying Vanessa and Laura for operational follow-up and to coordinate an SLA bridge conversation.

We will follow up with a short post-incident summary and next steps when the primary providers restore stable peering.

—Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Platform Reliability, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Service interruption in US/EU/APAC regions — immediate guidance

Hi Jesse — quick answers: 
- Session affinity: switching region preference will re-establish new WS/stream sessions. For in-flight streams, we recommend completing short-running streams and re-establishing new streams against the fallback region. If you must preserve affinity, keep a small subset (10–15%) pinned to the original region, but expect higher error rates.
- Automated fallbacks: they will remain active until we observe 30m of stable peering and healthy RPC latencies within normal thresholds. We will update the incident page when we remove them.
- Streaming chunk size: yes — reduce chunk size by ~40% for the next 2 hours to reduce tail amplification.

Actions we’ve taken on our side:
- Enabled cross-region proxying for affected customers and increased KV cache TTL to reduce repeated cold starts.
- Deployed a model-variant fallback (redwood-medium) for large-sequence requests to help keep percentiles low.

We’ll keep the HelioBank incident liaison (Jesse) updated. If anything breaks during the cutover, DM me on Slack and we’ll escalate to the provider.

—Markus

Subject: Internal: HelioBank incident — post-incident plan & timeline

Team — summarizing until the customer-facing postmortem: 
1) Timeline (high level)
- 07:58Z: Provider reported peering anomaly impacting several regions.
- 08:05Z: Automated health checks show elevated p99 latency and partial RPC failures for EU/ASIA zones.
- 08:12Z: Customer outbound notification sent (see thread).
- 08:45Z: Deployed regional fallback routing and model-variant downgrade.
- 09:50Z: Stabilization observed for US region; EU/APAC still showing intermittent packet loss on provider side.

2) Immediate follow-ups (owners)
- Dylan: collect and scrub telemetry for HelioBank from 07:30–11:00Z and populate incident doc.
- Vanessa: prepare SLA bridge packet + proposed credit window; attach the draft to the customer-facing postmortem.
- Laura: draft external postmortem with timeline, root cause, mitigation, and permanent remediation proposals.

3) Root cause hypothesis so far: an inter-region peering flap at the cloud provider caused asymmetric routing and packet drops that amplified backend RPC retries. Our mitigation bought time but we need a permanent fix — improved cross-region fast-paths and health-aware routing in the control plane.

Please update the incident doc with notes and add any customer-specific actions. I’m scheduling a 30-min sync at 13:00Z for the postmortem draft review.

—Markus
